title: Viewport-Aware Panel Anchoring and Modal Stabilization for Data-Dense Console Pages
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Some console pages with dense data (multi-column tables, live charts, and stacked modals) exhibit layout instability across browsers and breakpoints: header flicker when modals open, chart canvas truncation at narrow widths, and inconsistent column collapse behavior on small viewports. This causes confusion for users monitoring rollouts and cost dashboards and increases support load.

Goal: Define, prototype, and validate a set of CSS/interaction patterns and fallback behaviors so dashboards, rollouts, and cost views remain stable, readable, and interactive across Chrome, Firefox, Safari (desktop + iOS), and Edge. Deliverables: Figma responsive prototypes, a short interaction spec, cross-browser QA checklist, and a design review + signoff that maps to two small engineering tickets (layout primitives + modal stacking).

Scope: Focus on three surface families: 1) Data grids / wide tables with priority-based column collapse, 2) Time-series and stacked charts embedded in panels, 3) Multi-layer modals and flyouts used by rollouts and billing flows. We will not change visual design tokens or introduce new colors—this is layout/behavior only.

Constraints: Must work within existing console layout system and CSS variables. Engineering prefers minimal JS for layout fixes — prefer CSS-first solutions with optional light JS polyfills for legacy Safari fixes. Performance target: no jank on 2x CPU usage pages; avoid layout thrashing.

Files & links: Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/REDACTED/console-responsive-panels-proto
Design brief (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/UX/pages/REDACTED/Viewport+Anchoring+Spec
Reference GH PR (engineering stubs): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4892
Live bug examples (internal replay): https://observability.internal/redwood/replays/console-viewport-2333

Decisions & trade-offs: 1) Use 'contain: layout inline-size' on panel containers to limit reflow propagation (pro: isolates expensive layout; con: older Safari versions ignore contain flags). 2) Prefer 'position: sticky' for header anchoring with transform fallback where unsupported; implement small JS to polyfill sticky-to-translate conversion for affected browsers. 3) For charts, prefer canvas resizing using ResizeObserver with a debounce to avoid continuous re-layout. If ResizeObserver not available, fallback to window.resize listener (less ideal). 4) Table collapse chooses content-priority classes we already have (priority-1..4) instead of automatic truncation so product owners can control important columns.

Acceptance criteria: 1) On Chrome/Firefox/Safari/Edge desktop at widths 320px, 480px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px: panels do not overlap; modal z-index stacking is correct; page header remains visible without content shift > 8px when opening/closing modals. 2) Charts never clip important axis labels at breakpoints; legend collapses into a stacked badge at <420px. 3) Tables collapse columns deterministically: priority-1 columns always visible; horizontal scroll appears only when all columns are present and user opts in. 4) No console layout regressions reported in canary for console-2026.03. 5) Cross-browser checklist completed and signed off by engineering + QA.

Prototype notes: Created three responsive breakpoints in Figma: Compact (<=420px), Narrow (421-800px), Wide (801+). Interactions include: modal open/close, nested modal behavior (escape/backdrop), table column toggles, chart resize animation (150ms fade). We used low-fidelity micro-interactions to communicate easing and timing rather than final animations.

Accessibility notes: Ensure modal focus trap is preserved when using transform-based positioning polyfills. For table collapse, columns that hide must still be discoverable via the column toggler control and keyboard accessible. Color/contrast not changed in this scope.

Reviewers: PM - Ibrahim Patel; Eng lead - Saanvi Rao; Accessibility - Jonah Ruiz.

Sign-off criteria: All reviewers must approve Figma frames and the Confluence spec. Engineering must attach the small QA checklist as a PR requirement before merging layout changes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Panels stable across listed breakpoints and browsers with <=8px shift on modal open/close; 2) Charts retain axis/legend legibility at Compact/Narrow breakpoints; 3) Table column collapse honors priority-* classes and column toggler is keyboard operable; 4) ResizeObserver-backed chart resizing implemented with 150ms debounce; 5) Cross-browser QA checklist passed and signed by QA and Eng lead.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Maya Chen: Initial exploration prototype uploaded to Figma. Noted odd Safari behavior on iOS where position:sticky within a transformed parent is ignored — added note to spec for polyfill approach.

2026-02-25 - Liam O'Connor: Engineering feasibility review done. ENG work split into two tickets: one for layout primitives (ENG-6123) and one for chart resize/observer (ENG-6230). Suggested limiting use of contain: to specific heavy panels to avoid breaking A/B banner positioning.

2026-03-01 - Jonah Ruiz: Accessibility pass: modal focus trap verified in prototype. Added requirement that hidden columns remain accessible via a single 'Columns' menu with aria-controls and aria-expanded attributes.

2026-03-05 - Saanvi Rao: Implemented small CSS prototype in sandbox and found a repaint issue when toggling column visibility—will add requestAnimationFrame batching in the engineering ticket to avoid layout thrash.

2026-03-09 - Ibrahim Patel: PM review complete. Please add a note in Confluence about rollout strategy: canary to 10% of orgs observing metrics for 72 hours before full release. Also request that cost dashboards are prioritized due to billing team sensitivity.

2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connor: Updated engineering tasks: ENG-6123 now includes Safari polyfill and ENG-6230 includes ResizeObserver fallback. Ready for design sign-off pending minor wording updates in Figma frames.
next_steps: 1) Incorporate accessibility feedback into Figma and update Confluence spec (Maya). 2) Break down ENG-6123 into two subtasks—contain flags and sticky polyfill (Liam). 3) QA to create cross-browser checklist and run on the staging cluster (QA). 4) Schedule design review w/ Eng lead and PM for 2026-03-11; after sign-off, mark ticket as Done and move engineering tickets to Planned.
qa_checklist:
- Run Chrome/Firefox/Safari/Edge desktop tests at 320/480/768/1024/1440 widths
- Test iOS Safari on iPhone SE and iPhone 12
- Validate modal focus trap and keyboard navigation
- Verify chart axis and legend do not clip; axis labels readable
- Confirm table column toggler exposes hidden columns and keyboard operable
- Measure layout shift (CLS-like) on modal open; must be <=8px
- Run smoke tests for rollouts and billing routes to ensure no metric regressions
notes_for_engineering: Prefer CSS-first approach: contain + sticky + grid/flex fallbacks. Where necessary add narrowly-scoped JS polyfills (sticky -> translateY, ResizeObserver debounce). Avoid global resets. Tag PRs with 'layout-primitives' and attach cross-browser QA checklist. If performance regressions appear, revert contain usage on specific panels and try alternative isolation (will require close coordination with runtime team).
